description: Use when an ARC grid is mostly a background color with regularly spaced lattice lines and exceptional colors at line crossings. Infer the compact marker pattern from demonstrations.

# ARC lattice-marker compression

## Recognition
- The input may be a large mostly uniform grid with regularly spaced horizontal/vertical rails of a second color.
- Exceptional colors appear at selected rail intersections, often repeated in adjacent rows/columns or mirrored around the grid.
- The output can be a much smaller grid describing the arrangement of the exceptional markers; it is not necessarily a crop of the input.

## Method
1. Identify the dominant background and the regularly spaced rail rows/columns.
2. Record the colors at rail crossings (distinguish genuine marker colors from the rail color and background).
3. Compare the crossing pattern with the demonstrated output dimensions and values. Repeated adjacent crossing rows/columns may be redundant encoding; compress them to the demonstrated scale rather than copying every intersection literally.
4. Preserve marker colors and use the input background color for output positions with no marker. Use symmetries and repeated blocks as constraints.
5. On a test shaped like a simple repeated frame with the same marker color at all corners and no other markers, check whether the compact result is a single cell containing that marker; this mapping was confirmed for one instance.

## Caution
The precise compression/grouping is task-specific. Do not assume every crossing maps one-to-one to an output cell. Demonstrations showed repeated crossing patterns collapsing to smaller outputs (including background-valued cells), so infer the reduction using the demo output dimensions and compare multiple rows/columns before submitting.",
